describes: The town seen whole from the city camera (unity/Assets/Code/Editor/Town/LT1Town.cs, Light): one mean colour for each thing no single material record holds at that distance. That covers the ground's cover, the trees' crowns in late October, the lanes' surfaces and the boats' paints. It also says which paints and roofs the houses take from paint.json and materials/*.json. Nearer tiers draw the materials themselves.
notes: Cover tones are wet ground in late October on the Rogaland coast: grass still green in the mild wet autumn, heather rust-dark and dead bracken going brown in patches, grey gneiss with lichen in ledges along the banks and the heath; under the crowns of the trees that shed (birch, rowan, sycamore, apple) their fallen leaves lie wet, a warm brown below the grass's value (litter). Birch is past its yellow peak and one in four is bare (its twigs a grey-violet mass from afar), rowan has turned, and sycamore and apple are half green. The old lanes keep the old town's white (paint.json, schemes). A warehouse takes its period's back-of-house paints, falun red and ochre. A roof takes the covering of its year built. A neglected house's paint goes part way toward the soil's colour, as grime and chalking read from afar. A sjøhus has small windows along its sides and a stack of loading hatches in each gable, the port at the quay; the church tall windows along its sides and its door in the west gable. A porch has its door in its gable to the lane, glazed sides where its era glazed them; a lean-to one small window at its back. At 17:50 in late October most households are home and a room in two is lit: a lit window is the moment's (local scene state, seeded, claiming nothing), never in a house its diary says is empty or boarded; its light is the room's lamp on its walls and curtains (materials/glass.json), pane its brightness at a window glow of 1. By day a pane is dark glass, its sheen soft (smoothness, under the screen's reflections), never a frosted gradient. The quay's face is capped with a coping of dressed granite widthM wide standing heightM proud, and cast-iron bollards stand on it every everyM metres (quay), never where a sjøhus stands on the edge or a pier leaves it. It is the moment's (local scene state, seeded, claiming nothing). The harbour's water at this tier is a designed colour, not a mirror: the sky's hue, greener and lighter where the bed shows through shallow water, deepening to open water by deepM, darkest at the foot of a made thing (footM) as its shade and reflection lie there; one light line lineM wide at every waterline, round the shore, the quay, the piers, the sjøhus and every boat; above it on the quay's face, the piers and the feet of the sjøhus, a band wetM high darkened to wet of the stone's colour. It is a mirror for the screen's reflections (smoothness), at reflection of their strength, as still water gives back a darker world; parallel crests along the quay (waveScale of them per metre, wavering along their length over waveStretch of their spacing by up to waveWobble radians, their steepest slope waveStrength) break the mirror into bands, never into glitter. A boat's inside is not its hull's paint: an open boat's floor and sides are oiled wood (boatInside, open), a decked boat's deck a worn grey a step below its hull (decked), so from above a boat is its gunwale's pale rim round a darker inside. Hedges in late October: privet dark and still in leaf (two in four), hawthorn olive going thin, beech holding its copper leaves through the winter. The lanes' setts and gravel are lighter and warmer than the grass round them, as dry stone is, so the town's net of lanes and steps reads from the hill. The crowns sit a clear step below the walls and are muted, as wet October leaves are against white paint: the low sun warms them enough. A crown's edge is a fringe of leaf strokes (fringe): diamonds size times the mass's radius from centre to tip (by spread), width of that to each side and tail of it below, leaning up to turn radians, on a share of the upper facets of each mass, out of it by out of their size, their normals turned radial of the way from the facet's and jittered, their tones by tone; each turned to the eye and opened only where the crown turns from the eye (the facing between edge's two values), so the strokes break the outline and the sky seams and never the lit face. The masses' facets are shaded soften of the way turned to the mass's own round, taken from a point lift of its half height under its middle, so a crown reads as a lit and a shaded side with its planes a hint, not a cut gem, and its underside takes the sky's light as leaves let it through. A broadleaf's crown is its leaf clusters (clusters), as a branch's foliage masses: a core, and masses radiusM in radius set over the crown's envelope from its underside's edge to its top, as many as cover times its area over a mass's takes, up to most, round a core core of their tone, the crown's inside seen between them; each shaded whole of the way from its own round toward its crown's, and its leaf strokes turned to the crown's round, so a crown has one lit and one shaded side and its clusters show in its outline and the shadows they lay on each other, never as a pile of separate balls. The trunk forks into a limb for each low cluster. A trunk is its species' bark (trunks, or default), a birch's pale; it is girth of the tree's height across at its foot and half that where it enters the crown.
